Concentrated triage batch: `finding` → `pm:queue` + `domain:ui`, **Bug**, M — a published type that ships EMPTY of its named members: `StackSchema`'s Omit-of-FlexSchema collapses under `BaseSchema`'s index signature, so the shipped declaration carries only `type`. Fix at the mechanism (restructure so the Omit survives — explicit member interface, or lift the index signature out of the inheritance path the Omit crosses), and add the emitted-dts pin the card's measurement used so a future collapse reds. Note the body's sanitizer warning: re-derive the exact spellings from the repo, not from this card's prose.

## Claimed + dispatched — `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat

PM session `session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`, branch `claude/issue-6151-stackschema-omit-collapse`.
The assignee field does not establish whose claim this is — this comment's session ID does. No earlier claim comment exists.

### 裁决 (binding)

**Fix at the mechanism, not at the symptom.** `StackSchema` is a **published type that ships EMPTY of its named members** — its `Omit`-of-`FlexSchema` collapses under `BaseSchema`'s index signature, so the shipped declaration carries only `type`.

Restructure so **the `Omit` survives**: either an explicit member interface, or lift the index signature out of the inheritance path the `Omit` crosses. ⛔ Do not paper over it by re-declaring the members somewhere the collapse still happens downstream.

**Add the emitted-`.d.ts` pin the card's measurement used**, so a future collapse goes red. ⚠️ That pin is the deliverable as much as the fix — this defect was invisible precisely because nothing looked at the emitted declaration.

### ⚠️ Verify — the card warns about itself

Triage: *"Note the body's sanitizer warning: **re-derive the exact spellings from the repo, not from this card's prose**."* GitHub's comment sanitizer eats angle-bracket fragments, so generic parameters and `Omit<…>` spellings in the card text may be **mangled**. Read the source.

Also confirm: the collapse still reproduces on today's `main`; which members are supposed to survive; and that `BaseSchema`'s index signature is the actual cause (this repo's `BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()` with `[key: string]: any` — the #5155 structural ceiling — and it has produced surprising results twice tonight, including a dev correctly predicting a TS error that did **not** fire for exactly this reason).

### Traps

⚠️ **The pin must read the EMITTED `.d.ts`, not the source.** A source-level type assertion can pass while the emitted declaration is empty — that gap *is* this bug. Build the package, then assert against `dist`.

⚠️ **`tsc` resolves workspace deps through `dist` while `vitest` aliases to `src/`** — measured tonight. A type-check red can be unbuilt siblings, a real error, or both (a dev got 15 errors: 14 noise + 1 real). Build the closure first, then classify every remaining error by name.

⚠️ `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec vitest` / `cd packages/x && pnpm exec vitest` hit a guard (objectui#3378) — one form **refuses loudly**, another **silently runs `apps/console`'s 22 files and reports green**. **Always run vitest from the repo root.**

### Standing rules

Predict direction before running; prove mutations on disk by grepping injected AND separately removed text; print the landing site; assert anchor uniqueness; restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command and confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` empty. Derive gates by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**. A cached turbo green is not a measurement — `--force`. Commit before you ablate.

**Changeset**: a published type gains its declared members — state it in words. ⛔ Never `major`.

### Collision bounds

`packages/types` is yours. ⚠️ **#6105** (ADR-0049 `z.never()` tombstone `.describe()` text) is open in the same package and is **not yours** — different files expected; ⛔ report any same-file overlap rather than resolving it. Eight sibling agents are live elsewhere — ⛔ do not edit `packages/components/**`, `packages/plugin-form/**`, `packages/plugin-list/**`, `packages/plugin-detail/**`, `packages/core/**`, `packages/plugin-kanban/**`, `packages/plugin-map/**`, `packages/app-shell/src/utils/**`, `examples/schema-catalog/**`, `apps/site/**`.

⛔ Leave the PR **draft** — the PM lands it.

## ⛔ Correction: this card was NOT orphaned — PR #6267 exists. + review of that PR.

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01Mn4BZ5AVDM81pvfij1WwM9` (`os-litant`).

### What I got wrong, and how I caught it

I classified this as one of seven cards whose agent had died, and started opening a draft PR to rescue "unpushed work". **The API refused it: a PR already exists for this branch.** [PR #6267](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/6267), opened 06:05Z — and it had been sitting in the open-PR listing I read at 07:00Z, where I failed to connect it to this card.

⚠️ The near-miss is worth recording because it is the same shape as everything else today: I inferred "no PR" from **not having seen one**, rather than asking. Absence of an observation is not an observation of absence. ✅ The mechanical guard caught it, not my judgement.

The other six reclaims stand — those branches carry **zero content delta** and have no PR. This one is different in both respects.

**This stroke:** assignee → this seat, `pm:dispatched` retained. ⛔ Not a re-dispatch, ⛔ no new agent. The card is in **review**, not in flight.

### Review of PR #6267 — the work is excellent

⭐ **The ablation is the strongest I have reviewed in this lane.** Predicted **9 red / 4 green** before running; observed exactly that. And the four survivors are the *right* four — three are non-vacuity guards that exist to prove the population was read at all, and the fourth pins union discrimination, which this defect never broke. ✅ That is honest evidence grading, not a green screenshot.

⭐ **The pin reads the emitted declaration, and explains why it must.** A source-level assertion passes on the broken code — the index signature answers for the missing key with `any`, and `any` satisfies everything. **That gap is the bug**, so a guard that never opens the `.d.ts` cannot see it. It also declines to read `dist/` — because this repo's `test` job runs with no build step (`turbo`'s `test` only `dependsOn: ["^build"]`, and `packages/types` has no workspace deps, so nothing builds it), which would make a `dist`-reading guard **vacuous exactly where it is needed**. It compiles through the API into a scratch dir instead. That is the "degenerate control" trap identified and defended against by name.

⭐ **The scope check answers the class, not the instance.** Every `Omit` in `packages/types/src` measured against the built `dist`: three other heritage clauses healthy (they `Omit` over spec types carrying no index signature), and **two property-position `Omit`s that DO collapse** (`objectql.ts:1480/:1486`, `ObjectGridSchema` 61 → 0) — ⛔ deliberately **not** fixed here, because the correct replacement shape is a design question rather than a mechanical move. ✅ Filed separately rather than smuggled in. That is exactly the right call.

⭐ **The downstream sweep was narrowed with evidence, not by guess**: `FlexSchema`'s emitted member set is identical before and after and its members moved byte-identically, so only code naming `StackSchema` can be affected — three packages, all type-check green with the script name echoed in each run (guarding the zero-match-`--filter`-exits-0 trap).

**Gates read by name:** 27 checks — **24 `success`, 3 `skipped`, zero failures**, all `completed`.

### ⛔ Two blockers to landing — neither is a defect in the work

1. **`mergeable_state: unknown`, and the base is stale.** PR base is `ef2a3bd8d`; `main` has moved well past it. ⛔ `unknown` is not `clean` and is not a verdict. Needs a `main` merge and a re-read before any landing decision.

2. ⚠️ **A Clause-② tier call is owed, and I cannot make it.** The PR's own changeset reasoning is explicit that this **moves the accept set** of a published type: *"`gap: 'large'` on a stack node used to type-check through the index signature and is now a `tsc` error."* That is the mechanical Clause-② trigger. But **there is no claim comment on this card at all** — so no `Clause-②` declaration was ever recorded, and the tier the original dispatch ran at **died with the previous session**.

   ⛔ Unknown tier is not the same as sufficient tier. Treating "I can't see it" as "it's fine" is the exact fallacy this PR's own methodology rejects. So I am **not** landing it on my own authority.

✅ **The merits are not in question** — I would ACCEPT this on the work. What it needs is a tier ruling, not rework. Routed to the maintainer in the round report; the PR stays **draft** meanwhile.

**That reasoning was wrong, and I am reversing it explicitly rather than quietly.**

### Why — the question was already answered, in the record I maintain

Two standing maintainer orders, both carried on the seat post (objectui#5560) and both of which I had already transcribed there myself:

1. **「直接入队」** — Clause-② work in **this repo** goes at-tier and **straight to the queue**. ⚠️ `needs:contract-review` does not exist in objectui, so the compensating-label route is unavailable *by construction*, and that is precisely the situation the order was given for.
2. **「Fable 5 配额已耗尽，可以用 Opus 继续」** — fable is exhausted; opus is the recorded substitute. That is the skill's own **quota-exhaustion exemption**, whose stated condition is that the tier and its reason are recorded — which the claim comments do.

⇒ The chain is complete: fable unavailable → opus with the reason on the card → straight to the queue. **There was no open question. I raised one that the record had already closed, and held finished work on it.**

⚠️ Worth naming the shape, because it is the *inverse* of the error that dominated today. Everywhere else I over-trusted an inherited claim; here I under-trusted a recorded ruling and treated "I did not personally witness the dispatch" as "the gate is unmet." **Both are failures to read what is actually written.**

### What actually makes this Clause-② card safe

The skill is explicit that it is **not the tier** — it is the compensating evidence: *a verdict flip measured in both directions, pinned in tests, plus a downstream `tsc` sweep against the new `dist/*.d.ts`.* **This PR carries both, in full:**

- **The flip, both directions, against the EMITTED declaration** — `StackSchema` 1 → 25 declared properties, `FlexSchema` unchanged at 25 with its members moved byte-identically (`diff` exit 0). The pin reads the emitted `.d.ts`, never the source, and the PR explains why a source-level assertion would pass on the broken code.
- **Ablation predicted 9 red / 4 green, observed exactly** — and the four survivors are the correct four (three non-vacuity guards plus union discrimination, which the defect never touched).
- **The downstream sweep, narrowed with evidence rather than guessed** — only `StackSchema`'s shape changed, so only code naming it can be affected; that population is three packages, all type-check green with the script name echoed to guard the zero-match-`--filter`-exits-0 trap.

**27 checks — 24 `success`, 3 `skipped`, zero failures**, all `completed`, read ~50 minutes after the run started. Base merged up to current `main`; head now `e51f5ea93`.

### Disposition

Flipping ready and enqueuing. Path face is `packages/types/**` + `.changeset/` — ⛔ no governed surface.
